pr_comments: I believe we should be addressing this particular problem https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/77192#issuecomment-1058159370 rather than working around the non-recursion support. By changing the redirection this will fail when people continue to have the older collection installed before it was redirected in that collection. Fixing the double redirection as mentioned in that comment will have it support older collection alongside newer collection versions.
This is a breaking change for lots of users. We need to get the fix back ported to 2.9, 2.11 and 2.12 and have them released as soon as we can. @ashwini-mhatre @cidrblock @sivel @jborean93

2.9 will not get a fix for this as 2.9 is in security only phase.  You may need to document for users of 2.9 that they need to use an older netcommon release.

At earliest, 2.11 and 2.12 would get the bug fix on March 28.

It may be advantageous to revert your change to netcommon until we can address the bug.
@ashwini-mhatre @Qalthos @trishnaguha I opened a PR based on sivel's proposed fix. If you can test it out, I'd appreciate it: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/77210

Oh, fwiw, that patch was made with `git diff -w` so it's not showing the whitespace changes.

I've updated my patch from above a little, to use range, and raise a proper error if we exceed the max redirect count, which I arbitrarily set at 30.

I don't have the bandwidth right now to see this change through.  It'll require someone to complete the patch, add proper tests, and a changelog.

Ideally the code that follows redirects should probably be moved to it's own function, and to check recursive redirects, we should compare to previous redirects, and not put a limit on depth.
